title: ast.parse can crash with an uncaught RecursionError, breaking the AC-7 one-line-refusal contract
body: _python_entries only catches (SyntaxError, ValueError) around ast.parse (skeleton.py:247). A syntactically valid but deeply nested Python file (e.g. a long chained `1+1+1+...` expression, well under skeleton.max_bytes) makes ast.parse raise RecursionError. Verified end-to-end: `python3 scripts/klc skeleton deep.py` with PROJECT_ROOT pointed at a scratch directory (a 400 KB file with 200 000 '+' terms) prints a full Python traceback to stderr, nothing to stdout, exit code 1. AC-7 promises 'exactly one line `<path>: <reason>` and exit 1, never an empty body' for every refusal case; a traceback is neither the one-line format nor an honest reason, and stdout is empty. This is a real, reproducible gap, not a contrived one — generated source or long data literals are exactly the kind of file an agent would run `klc skeleton` on first.
fix: Catch RecursionError (and consider MemoryError) around ast.parse (and around ast.unparse/entry-building, which walks the same tree) in _python_entries, and raise _Refusal('syntax errors — read the file instead') or a dedicated reason. Add a deeply-nested-expression fixture to tests/test_klc139_skeleton_refusals.py.

title: A UTF-8-BOM-prefixed Python file is falsely refused as 'syntax errors'
body: The Python path decodes with `.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` (skeleton.py:385), not `utf-8-sig`, so a leading BOM (0xEF 0xBB 0xBF) survives into the str as U+FEFF. `ast.parse` treats a leading U+FEFF as invalid and raises SyntaxError, which _python_entries turns into 'syntax errors — read the file instead'. Verified independently: a BOM-prefixed `import os\ndef f(): pass` (a file `python3 bom.py` itself runs fine) is refused by skeleton() with exit 1 and that exact reason. BOM-prefixed .py files are a realistic case (common output of Windows editors/tools; the repo itself ships klc-completion.ps1 for Windows users). This is worse than a crash: it looks like a legitimate, confident refusal, so an agent has no signal that the file is actually fine and will avoid reading it or conclude the file is broken.
fix: Decode with `errors="replace"` after first stripping a leading '\ufeff', or decode with 'utf-8-sig' when no other errors mode is needed. Add a BOM fixture to tests/test_klc139_skeleton_python.py or _refusals.py asserting exit 0 and a normal outline.

title: A non-UTF-8 non-Python file that ast-grep skips is dishonestly reported as 'unsupported language'
body: ast-grep 0.42.1 skips a file it cannot decode as UTF-8: its --inspect stderr then has a `summary|file:` sentinel (so the current 'no inspect output' check does not fire) but no `entity|file` line for that file. `_astgrep_entries` treats 'no entity|file line' the same as 'this extension has no rule coverage' and refuses `unsupported language: <ext>` (skeleton.py:353-355). Verified: a .ts file with a raw 0xE9 byte inside an expression is refused `unsupported language: .ts`, even though TypeScript is fully covered by the generic profile. This is the same 'dishonest reason' problem as the BOM finding, on the non-Python path: the reported cause (no rule for this extension) is factually wrong, which could send an agent hunting for a rule-coverage gap that does not exist.
fix: Distinguish the two 'no entity|file line' causes. When the sentinel line itself reports `skippedFileCount >= 1` (or similar) for this scan, refuse with something like 'ast-grep failed (file not decodable — read the file instead)' instead of 'unsupported language'. Add a non-UTF-8 .ts/.rs fixture to tests/test_klc139_skeleton_refusals.py.

title: An unreadable file (PermissionError/OSError) crashes instead of producing a clean refusal
body: skeleton()'s only handler is `except _Refusal`. `real.stat()` and `real.read_bytes()` (lines 375 and 385) can raise PermissionError (a chmod-000 file, verified directly: `sk.skeleton(path)` raises `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied`) or other OSErrors (EIO, a file removed between the is_file() check and the read). Same AC-7 contract break as the RecursionError finding: no one-line reason, and depending on where the traceback happens, no exit-1-with-refusal-text at all.
fix: Wrap the stat()/read_bytes() calls in `except OSError as e: raise _Refusal(...)`, reusing or extending the 'not a file' wording, and add a permission-denied refusal test (skip on platforms where chmod 000 has no effect, e.g. when running as root).

title: The Python header's line count (str.splitlines()) can overcount relative to ast/editor line numbers
body: `len(text.splitlines())` (skeleton.py:386) splits on \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, \u2028 and \u2029 in addition to \n/\r\n/\r, while `ast` (and hence every range in the outline) counts only newlines. A form-feed character or a U+2028 inside a string literal inflates the header's reported line count above what any entry's end range, or the file's actual line count in an editor, would show. Ranges themselves are unaffected — only the header's '(python, N lines)' claim can be wrong.
fix: Count lines with something that matches ast's notion of a line break, e.g. `text.count("\n") + (1 if text and not text.endswith("\n") else 0)`, adjusted for a lone trailing \r file.
